newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks fines on Germany, Italy over green laws.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks fines on Germany, Italy over green laws.

text.p: The European Commission asked the European Court on Wednesday to fine Germany and Italy for not complying with EU environmental law.

"The European Commission decided to make applications to the European Court of Justice against Germany and Italy for failing to comply with previous court judgements for infringing European Union environmental law," a statement said.

"It also decided that in making these applications, it will for the first time ask the court to impose financial penalties which the court obtained the power to do under the Maastricht treaty," it said.
The daily penalties against Germany, which relate to rules on protecting birds, ground and surface water, are for 26,400 Ecus, 264,000 Ecus and 158,400 Ecus respectively.
The Commission proposed daily fines for Italy related to waste and radiation protection of 123,900 Ecus and 159,300 Ecus.

"I see it as extremely important that the Commission here for the first time has come out with proposals for financial penalties. These cases will serve as important precendents," said European Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard.
One Commission official, who asked not to be named, said that altogether about 30 cases of EU states not applying Union law were being considered for possible fines.
Among files closest to a decision were four cases against Belgium, one against Greece, one against Luxembourg and six against France, the official said.
The fines will only become due after the Court upholds the Commission's applications, which it might not even consider for months.
"It could take quite a while unfortunately," Bjerregaard's spokesman Peter Jorgensen told a news conference.
